title: Everolimus Post-Bland Hepatic Artery Embolization in Patients With Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs) With Liver Metastasis
official: Phase 2 Dose Optimization Trial of Everolimus Post-Bland Hepatic Artery Embolization (Evero-Embo) in Patients With Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs) With Liver Metastasis
summary: This study is being done to learn whether people with neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) that have spread to the liver can safely tolerate a lower dose of everolimus after bland hepatic artery embolization (HAE).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients must have histologically or cytologically confirmed Grade 1 or 2 NET with measurable liver metastasis (≥1.0 cm).
* Morphologically progressive disease by RECIST 1.1 and/or ≥25% but ≤75% tumor burden in the liver.
* Prior tolerance of at least 5 mg daily everolimus for ≥5 days pre-HAE. NOTE: There is no maximum amount of time a patient may be taking Everolimus before HAE as the study focuses on after the pre-HAE dose is established.
* Prior therapy: Patients are eligible regardless of the number or type of prior therapies and without a requirement to have received a specific therapy prior to enrollment. Patients will take everolimus leading up to the embolization once enrolled in the study. They will only be enrolled in the study for their first hepatic artery embolization. They must be 30 days out since their last cancer treatment of any kind, not including somatostatin analogs.
* Age ≥18 years.
* ECOG performance status ≤2 (see Appendix A).
* Patients must have adequate organ and marrow function as defined below:
* absolute neutrophil count ≥1,000/mcL
* platelets ≥100,000/mcL
* total bilirubin ≤ institutional upper limit of normal (ULN)
* Child-Turcotte-Pugh class A; B dose reduction is recommended at 5mg QD or less; C recommend non-usage of everolimus
* Creatinine (or GFR) ≤ institutional ULN (Appendix B)
* GFR, glomerular filtration rate (or creatinine) There are no dose reductions required for patients in any stage of renal failure for everolimus
* Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-infected patients on effective anti-retroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible for this trial.
* For patients with evidence of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, the HBV viral load must be undetectable on suppressive therapy, if indicated.
* Patients with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection must have been treated and cured. For patients with HCV infection who are currently on treatment, they are eligible if they have an undetectable HCV viral load.
* Patients with a prior malignancy whose natural history or treatment does not have the potential to interfere with the safety or efficacy assessment of the investigational regimen are eligible for this trial.
* Patients with known history or current symptoms of cardiac disease, or history of treatment with cardiotoxic agents, should have a clinical risk assessment of cardiac function using the New York Heart Association Functional Classification. To be eligible for this trial, patients should be class 2B or better.
* Ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document. Legally authorized representatives may sign and give informed consent on behalf of study participants.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who have not recovered from adverse events due to prior anti-cancer therapy (i.e., have residual toxicities \> Grade 1) with the exception of alopecia.
* Prior transhepatic artery embolization.
* Contraindication to arteriography or embolization.
* Prior chemotherapy or peptide receptor radionuclide therapy within 1 month.
* Biliary stent or choledocho-enteric anastomosis.
* Patients who are receiving any other investigational agents for the treatment of this cancer.
* History of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to everolimus
* Concomitant medications: Patients should only be excluded from trial participation when clinically relevant known or predicted drug-drug interactions or potential overlapping toxicities will impact safety or efficacy. Drug-drug interactions of risk level X will be excluded from the trial unless an alternative medication can be substituted. Drug-drug interactions are classified into classes A, B, C, D and X. A Class X drug interaction represents a high-risk, contraindicated combination where the risks of taking the medications together clearly outweigh any potential benefits. These medications include Antihepaciviral Combination Products, BCG Products, Brivudine, Chikungunya Vaccine (Live), Chloramphenicol (Systemic), Cladribine, Dengue Tetravalent Vaccine (Live), Etrasimod, Fexinidazole, Grapefruit Juice, Inhibitors of CYP3A4 (Strong) and P-glycoprotein, Mumps- Rubella- or Varicella-Containing Live Vaccines, Nadofaragene Firadenovec, Natalizumab, Pimecrolimus, Pimozide, Poliovirus Vaccines (Live/Oral), Tacrolimus (Topical), Talimogene Laherparepvec, Tertomotide, Thiamphenicol, Typhoid Vaccine, Vaccines (Live), Yellow Fever Vaccine, Zoster Vaccine (Live/Attenuated). Additionally, patients should avoid taking everolimus while on strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. They should have everolimus dose reduction to 2.5 mg PO while on moderate CYP34A inhibitors and/or PgP inhibitors. An increase in everolimus dose is recommended when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer (see package insert, Appendix C).
* Patients with uncontrolled intercurrent illness.
* Pregnant women are excluded from this study because everolimus is an mTOR inhibitor agent with the potential for teratogenic or abortifacient effects. Because there is an unknown but potential risk for adverse events in nursing infants secondary to treatment of the mother with everolimus, breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with everolimus. NOTE: Patients treated with everolimus should use highly effective birth control during treatment and for 8 weeks after their last everolimus dosing. Male patients with female partners of reproductive potential should be advised to use effective contraception during treatment with everolimus and for 4 weeks after the last dose
